definitions.explanation: A building constructed with five stories. A standard example of the 〜{階|かい}{建|だ}て counter pattern, which describes how many floors a building has.

examples.japanese: {五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧だ。
⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{建|た}った→建つ：12544_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: A new five-story building went up in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{団地|だんち}→団地：04054_danchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦エレベーター→エレベーター：01340_erebeetaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Old five-story housing complexes often don't have elevators.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧ (five) + ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ (floor counter) + {建|だ}て (constructed). One member of the productive 〜⟦{階|かい}{建|だ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧ pattern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧: five-story apartment building
- {五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧: five-story building
- {五階建|ごかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{団地|だんち}→団地：04054_danchi⟧: five-story public housing

RELATED PATTERNS:
- ⟦{二|に}{階|かい}{建|だ}て→二階建て：03001_nikaidate⟧: two-story
- ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧⟦{階|かい}{建|だ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧: three-story
- ⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧⟦{階|かい}{建|だ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧ / ⟦{高層|こうそう}ビル→高層ビル：16994_kousoubiru⟧: high-rise building
- ⟦{平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て→平屋建て：28473_hirayadate⟧: single-story (irregular — no ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many older Japanese ⟦{団地|だんち}→団地：04054_danchi⟧ (public housing complexes) built in the 1960s-70s are five-story walk-ups, since buildings up to five floors were not required by law to have elevators.
